transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well, I guess I'm here because... I've been having some trouble with food lately. It's mostly at night. After everyone goes to bed, I... I tell myself I'm just going to have some leftovers. But then I sort of... I realize I've eaten half a tray of catered pasta from a work thing, the dessert from a client dinner, and just... whatever snacks are in the pantry. All in one sitting. So... yeah. That's why I came in.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating when this happens at night?

Not really. Um... once I start, it just... it feels like the decision-making part of me goes offline. Especially if things were tense with my husband that evening, I just... I keep reaching for more. Even when I'm sitting there thinking to myself, 'Patricia, stop, this is enough.' I just don't.
After these nighttime eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives to try to undo the effects of what you've eaten?
No. Um... no, I don't do anything like that. I just... no.
How often do these nighttime eating episodes happen?

Um... well, it's been going on for a little while now. Maybe... the last three months or so. I'd say it happens at least once a week. Usually after... well, if my husband and I had a disagreement, or if I had a late work thing. And, um... sometimes it's twice a week. But yeah, at least once.
Do you feel guilty or ashamed after these nighttime eating episodes?

Um... yeah. Yeah, I do. I just... I feel really embarrassed. And, um... disgusted with myself, honestly. I try so hard to be disciplined in every other part of my life, and then... it just feels like I blew it. I just sit there afterward and think... I don't know, I think about how I should have just gone for a run, or... or done yoga instead of doing that. It's... it's not a good feeling.
Do you ever find that you can't remember what you ate or how much you ate during these nighttime episodes?
No. Um... I remember. I know what I ate.
Do you find yourself eating more than usual during the day, before these nighttime episodes happen?
No... not really. I don't think so. I usually eat normally during the day.
Do you usually feel anxious or upset before these nighttime eating episodes happen?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think I feel anxious or anything beforehand. It just... happens.
Do you ever feel like you've lost control of your eating during the day?
No... not during the day. I'm usually just at work, so... no. It's fine then.
Do you ever have episodes like the ones you described at night, but during the day?
No... I don't. Like I mentioned, it's really just... at night. During the day is fine.
Have these nighttime eating episodes caused problems for you at work or in your relationships?

Um... work is fine. I'm still keeping up with everything there. It's mostly just... the mornings after those nights, I feel really drained. And... I guess, ashamed. So I've been skipping some things lately, like... my yoga class, or just plans with people. I just... I don't really want to face anyone right now.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since these nighttime eating episodes started?
Um... no. Not really. I don't... I haven't been checking my weight or anything, so... I guess I haven't noticed anything significant.
Do you feel like you're eating really quickly during these nighttime episodes?

Um... yeah, I suppose I do. I usually just... stand at the kitchen island. Or I'm scrolling through work emails, so... it's fast. I barely even taste it. Sometimes I just look down and... the containers are empty. Before I really even registered what I was eating.
Do you think you're eating at night because you're feeling emotional, like stressed or upset, and the food makes you feel better for a little while?
I don't know. I mean... maybe? I just... I get home and I'm tired. I don't really think about why I'm doing it. I just... do it.
Do you think eating at night helps you feel better when you're stressed or upset?
Um... I don't know. Like I said, I don't really think about it like that. I'm not sure it actually makes me feel better... it's just something that happens.
Do you think eating at night is a way for you to cope with feelings of stress or upset from your day?
I... I think you just asked me that. I really don't know if it's about coping. I just... I work a long day, I come home, and it happens. I'm not really sitting there thinking about my feelings.
Do you think the eating at night is related to feeling overwhelmed or upset about something that happened during the day?

I... I really don't have a different answer for you. You keep asking me the same thing. Like I said, I don't sit there and think about my day or being overwhelmed. I'm just tired. I don't know what else to tell you.
Do you feel like you're eating at night because you feel a strong urge to do so, and you can't stop yourself?

I mean... yeah, I guess that's closer to it. It's not about sitting around feeling sad, it's just... once I start... especially if, I don't know, things are tense with my husband that night or something... it just feels like the decision-making part of me goes offline. 

I'll just keep reaching for more, even while I'm literally thinking to myself, 'Patricia, stop, this is enough.' But I just don't.
Do you think your nighttime eating is usually triggered by feeling upset or emotional?
I... we just talked about this. I already said I don't know if it's about being upset. I'm just... I'm not really sure what else you want me to say about it.
Do you think your nighttime eating happens because you're trying to make yourself feel better when you're in a certain emotional state?
I... look, I feel like we're just going in circles now. I don't think it's about trying to make myself feel better. Like I just said, I don't really know. I don't have anything else to add to that.
